title: Rex: Closing the language-verifier gap with safe and usable kernel extensions
problem: Kernel extensions require manual verification and are error-prone; there is a significant gap between what high-level programming languages provide and what formal verification tools require, forcing developers to choose between safety and usability.
motivation: Kernel extensions are critical for system performance and flexibility, but unsafe code can compromise system integrity and reliability.
method: Rex provides a domain-specific language and compiler infrastructure that bridges high-level programming abstractions with formal verification requirements. The approach likely uses type systems or intermediate representations to automatically derive safety properties and enable efficient verification of kernel code while maintaining developer usability.
key_novelty: Unified framework that simultaneously provides programmer-friendly abstractions while maintaining formal verifiability guarantees for kernel extensions.
contributions: Language design bridging usability and verifiability for kernel extensions
Compiler and verification infrastructure for safe kernel development
Practical demonstration of formally verified kernel extensions
Reduced friction between writing and verifying kernel code
limitations: Not discussed; specific baselines, metrics, and detailed limitations require reading the full paper.
primary_theme: Safe and usable kernel extensions through language-verifier integration
